title: In re Rudy Pamintuan, Case No. 25-159C (LG's Office Chief of Staff)
text:
STATE OF NEVADA
BEFORE THE NEVADA COMMISSION ON ETHICS
In re Rudy Pamintuan, Chief of Staff, Ethics Complaint
Nevada Lieutenant’s Governor’s Office, Case No. 25-159C
State of Nevada, Confidential
______________________Subject /
STIPULATED AGREEMENT
1. PURPOSE: This Stipulated Agreement resolves Ethics Complaint Case No.
25-159C before the Nevada Commission on Ethics (“Commission”) Rudy Pamintuan
(“Pamintuan”), Chief of Staff for Lieutenant Governor Stavros Anthony.
2. JURISDICTION: At all material times, Pamintuan served as Chief of Staff for the
current Lieutenant Governor Stavros Anthony and was a public employee as defined in
NRS 281A.150. The Ethics in Government Law (“Ethics Law”) set forth in NRS Chapter
281A gives the Commission jurisdiction over elected and appointed public officers and
public employees whose conduct is alleged to have violated the provisions of NRS
Chapter 281A. See NRS 281A.280. The Commission has jurisdiction over Pamintuan in
this matter.
3. PROCEDURAL HISTORY BEFORE COMMISSION:
a. On September 9, 2025, the Commission initiated Ethics Complaint No. 25-
159C alleging violations of NRS 281A.400(2) and (7).
b. On September 9, 2025, the Commission issued its Order Initiating a
Complaint and on Jurisdiction and Investigation regarding the Complaint’s alleged
violations of NRS 281A.400(2) and (7).
c. On October 15, 2025, Pamintuan provided a timely response to the
allegations.
d. A Review Panel Determination issued on November 13, 2025, found the

facts established credible evidence to support a determination that just and sufficient
cause exists for the Commission to render an opinion in the matter regarding the alleged
violations of NRS 281A.400(2) and (7).
e. On November 17, 2025, Pamintuan submitted a signed waiver regarding
the time requirements for an adjudicatory hearing and the parties agreed to attend a
settlement conference.
f. In lieu of an adjudicatory hearing before the Commission, the parties
reached an agreement to resolve this matter on the terms reflected in this Stipulated
Agreement (“Agreement”) and now enter into this Agreement.
4. STIPULATED FACTS:
a. At all material times Pamintuan served as Chief of Staff for the Nevada
Lieutenant Governor.
b. From April 2023 and at all material times Pamintuan served as Treasurer of
Pioneer Technology & Arts Academy (“PTAA”), a nonprofit educational management
organization registered in Nevada.
c. Pamintuan has used some of his governmental time, staff, and equipment
to work on PTAA matters that included organizing a visit from Secretary of Education
Linda McMahon to Future Edge Academy, a contract partner of PTAA.
d. In January and February of 2025, Pamintuan had written to the Arizona
State University inquiring about an ROTC interview for his son and requesting information
about potential scholarships, and in addition, at around the same time, Pamintuan wrote
to the DMV requesting assistance with an issue he had with the DMV. These
correspondences were made by Pamintuan using his official state email account.
5. TERMS / CONCLUSIONS OF LAW: Based on the foregoing, Pamintuan and the
Commission agree as follows:
a. Each of the stipulated facts enumerated in Section 5 of this Agreement is
agreed to by the parties.
b. Pamintuan is a public employee as defined in NRS 281A.150.
c. Pamintuan has a commitment in a private capacity to his son pursuant to
NRS 281A.065(3) and to the PTAA Board pursuant to NRS 281A.065(5) and (6).
Stipulated Agreement
Case No. 25-159C
Page 2 of 6

d. Pamintuan stipulates that his conduct constitutes one non-willful violation of
the Ethics Law, implicating the provisions of NRS 281A.400(7) (prohibiting the use of
governmental time, property, equipment or other facility to benefit a significant personal
or pecuniary interest). See e.g. In re Prudhont, Comm’n Op. No. 22-033C, 22-034C
(2022); In re Matson, Comm’n Op. No. 11-67C (2014); see also In re Antinoro, Comm’n
Op. No. 16-54C (2017) (use of county resources for personal purposes improper “even
where no monetary benefit accrued”).
e. The alleged violations of NRS 281A.400(2) are hereby dismissed by
stipulation of the parties.
f. Based upon the consideration and application of the statutory factors set
forth in NRS 281A.775, Pamintuan and the Commission agree that pursuant to NRS
281A.170 one non-willful violation will be imposed for his violation of NRS 281A.400(7)
for the following reasons:
1. Seriousness of Violation: The Commission has recognized the
importance of avoiding the use of State resources to advance or attend to
personal matters, even if no direct financial gain occurs. Pamintuan’s use
of his official state email account and his government time for personal
matters creates an appearance of impropriety.
2. Previous History: Pamintuan has not previously been the subject of any
violation of the Ethics Law.
3. Cost of Investigation and Proceedings: Pamintuan was willing to resolve
the matter prior to an adjudicatory hearing, preserving Commission
expenses.
4. Prompt correction of the violation: There was no self-reporting or self-
correction in this matter, but Pamintuan was cooperative.
5. Additional Factors: None.
g. Pamintuan agrees to pay a civil penalty of $1,000.00 pursuant to NRS
281A.790(3) within one year of the approval of this agreement consistent with any payment
plan established by the Executive Director.
h. Pamintuan agrees to successfully complete Ethics Law training as approved
by the Executive Director within 60 days.
i. Pursuant to NRS 281A.785(2)(a), the Commission admonishes Pamintuan
that he must refrain from using state email systems for private business.
Stipulated Agreement
Case No. 25-059C
Page 3 of 7

j. This Agreement is based on the specific facts, circumstances, and law now
before the Commission. Facts or circumstances that differ from those present in this
matter may create a different resolution.
k. This Agreement is not intended to be applicable to or create any admission
of liability by Pamintuan for any other proceeding against or involving Pamintuan, and
such use is prohibited to the extent permitted by the jurisdiction of the Commission. If the
Commission rejects this Agreement, none of the provisions therein shall be considered by
the Commission or be admissible as evidence in a hearing on the merits in this matter.
6. WAIVER
a. Pamintuan knowingly and voluntarily waives his right to a hearing before the
full Commission on the allegations in Ethics Complaint Case No. 25-159C and all rights
he may be accorded with in regard to this matter pursuant to NRS Chapter 281A, the
regulations of the Commission (NAC Chapter 281A), the Nevada Administrative
Procedures Act (NRS Chapter 233B), and any other applicable provisions of law.
b.
Pamintuan knowingly and voluntarily waives his right to any judicial review
of this matter as provided in NRS Chapter 281A, NRS Chapter 233B, or any other applicable
provisions of law.
Stipulated Agreement
Case No. 25-159C

7.
ACCEPTANCE: We, the undersigned parties, have read this Agreement, understand
each and every provision therein, and agree to be bound thereby once approved by
the Commission. In addition, the parties orally agreed to be bound by the terms of this
Agreement during the regular meeting of the Commission on March 18, 2026.1
8. APPROVAL: Having reviewed the proposed stipulation by the parties, the
Commission approves findings of facts, conclusions of law, and terms of this
stipulation and directs the Executive Director to ensure compliance with this
agreement.
